nodes.name: Notifications & Communication
nodes.purpose: Deliver timely, warm, and actionable notifications to workers, clients, anonymous clients, and admins — triggered by every meaningful state transition in the platform.
nodes.ux_intent: Notifications feel like a trusted friend keeping you in the loop — not a corporate alert system. Every message is personal, clear, and tells you exactly what to do next.
outputs: delivered notifications via email | SMS | WhatsApp | in-app push
nodes.vertical_notes: Caregiving/cleaning specifics: job-start reminders (parent needs to know nanny is on the way), check-in/check-out confirmations, credential expiry alerts, safeguarding reminders. WhatsApp is primary channel in many markets — must support it alongside SMS.
open_questions: Should nannies get push notifications on mobile app?

nodes.name: Notification Dispatcher
nodes.purpose: Listen to platform events and route the right notification to the right person via the right channel, applying the org's communication cadence rules.
nodes.ux_intent: Dispatching is invisible to the user — notifications just arrive at the right time, through the channel they prefer, without duplication or spam.

nodes.name: Route Event to Recipient(s)
nodes.purpose: Determine who should be notified for a given event, apply the comm-cadence rules, and dispatch the right message(s) to the right channel(s).
nodes.ux_intent: A parent gets one clean message that their nanny is on the way — not three separate emails from different triggers.
nodes.vertical_notes: For anon clients: email or SMS only (no in-app). Messages should use warm, personal language: 'Hi Sarah, your cleaner Maria is confirmed for Tuesday at 10am.'

nodes.name: Retry Failed Notifications
nodes.purpose: Retry delivery of failed notifications with exponential backoff, and escalate to alternate channel if primary channel continues to fail.
nodes.ux_intent: The user never knows a retry happened — they just receive the message.

nodes.name: Send Email Notification
nodes.purpose: Render and deliver a notification via email, handling both authenticated users and anonymous clients who only have an email address.
nodes.ux_intent: Email reads like a personal note, not a system alert — first name, clear action, warm tone.
nodes.vertical_notes: Anon client emails: include a 'view your booking' link with token — no login required.

nodes.name: Send SMS Notification
nodes.purpose: Deliver a short, actionable notification via SMS to a phone number — used for anon clients and as a fallback for users who haven't enabled push.
nodes.ux_intent: SMS is short, direct, and feels urgent when it needs to — 'Your cleaner is on the way. See details: [link]'
nodes.vertical_notes: Primary channel for anon clients and for workers in markets where SMS is dominant. WhatsApp upgrade should be considered.

nodes.name: Send In-App / Push Notification
nodes.purpose: Deliver a real-time in-app notification and Web Push to authenticated users who have an active session or push subscription.
nodes.ux_intent: In-app notifications appear as a gentle badge and a slide-in banner — unobtrusive but immediately actionable.

nodes.name: Notification Templates
nodes.purpose: Manage the library of notification templates — one per event × channel combination — with vertical-specific copy for caregiving and cleaning.
nodes.ux_intent: Admins can see and customise what messages go out without touching code — the template editor is as simple as editing a text message.
nodes.vertical_notes: Templates pre-seeded for nanny/cleaning vertical. Examples: 'Your nanny {{worker_name}} is on the way and will arrive at {{eta}}. She'll check in when she arrives.' / 'Your cleaner has checked out. Your invoice for {{amount}} is attached.'

nodes.name: List Notification Templates
nodes.purpose: Show admin all notification templates for their org with the event they trigger and the channel they use.
nodes.ux_intent: Admin sees a clear table: 'Nanny on the way → SMS → [edit]'. No jargon, no technical field names.

nodes.name: Render Template
nodes.purpose: Substitute event variables into a template to produce the final notification body for delivery.
nodes.ux_intent: The output message reads naturally — 'Hi Sarah' not 'Hi {{client.first_name}}'.

nodes.name: Edit Notification Template
nodes.purpose: Allow admin to customise the copy of a notification template while maintaining the required variable slots.
nodes.ux_intent: Editing a template feels like editing a text message — a WYSIWYG preview shows how the final message will look with real data.
nodes.vertical_notes: Platform ships with a warm, caregiving-appropriate default copy. Admin can brand it but should be guided to keep it personal.

nodes.name: Notification Preferences
nodes.purpose: Let each person choose which notifications they receive and on which channels, without exposing technical channel names.
nodes.ux_intent: The preferences screen uses plain language: 'Tell me when a new job is offered to me' — not 'Subscribe to assignment.proposed via push'.

nodes.name: Get User Notification Preferences
nodes.purpose: Return the notification channel preferences for a person, used by the dispatcher to filter delivery channels.
nodes.ux_intent: Fully transparent — user can see at any time exactly what notifications they'll get and how.

nodes.name: Update Notification Preferences
nodes.purpose: Save a person's channel preferences for specific notification types.
nodes.ux_intent: Toggle switches that save instantly — no 'save' button needed.

nodes.name: In-App Notification Inbox
nodes.purpose: Provide an authenticated user with a persistent inbox of all past notifications they've received, so they never lose an important message.
nodes.ux_intent: The inbox feels like a clean conversation history — grouped by type, clearly dated, with a one-tap action on each message.

nodes.name: List Inbox Notifications
nodes.purpose: Retrieve paginated notification history for a user, with unread count for the badge.
nodes.ux_intent: Loads instantly with a small unread dot — user knows at a glance if anything needs attention.

nodes.name: Mark Notification as Read
nodes.purpose: Mark one or all notifications as read when the user views them.
nodes.ux_intent: Happens automatically when user opens the inbox — no extra tap needed to clear the badge.

nodes.name: Direct Messaging
nodes.purpose: Enable direct one-to-one messaging between an admin and a worker or client within the platform — avoiding the need to exchange personal phone numbers.
nodes.ux_intent: Feels like a familiar chat interface — worker and admin can quickly coordinate without leaving the app or sharing private contact details.
nodes.vertical_notes: Especially valuable for caregiving: parent can message nanny to say 'running 10 minutes late' without sharing personal numbers. All messages are logged for safeguarding purposes.
open_questions: Should messages be retained for safeguarding after assignment ends?

nodes.name: Send Direct Message
nodes.purpose: Create and deliver a direct message from one platform member to another within the context of an assignment or organisation.
nodes.ux_intent: Sending feels instant — the message appears immediately in the conversation thread with a subtle 'sent' tick.
nodes.vertical_notes: Cleaners can receive last-minute instructions via message (access codes, parking info). Nannies get check-in instructions. All logged.

nodes.name: View Message Thread
nodes.purpose: Retrieve the full message history between two parties, optionally scoped to a specific assignment.
nodes.ux_intent: The thread loads immediately with the latest messages visible — no pagination needed for short threads, infinite scroll for long ones.

nodes.name: Scheduled / Cadence Notifications
nodes.purpose: Run recurring background jobs that evaluate the org's communication cadence rules and dispatch reminders at the right time.
nodes.ux_intent: Users receive timely reminders without anyone having to remember to send them — the platform does the remembering.
nodes.vertical_notes: Critical for caregiving: 'Reminder: your nanny Mary is due tomorrow at 8am. Reply to confirm or call us if plans have changed.' Cleaners: 'Your clean is scheduled for Thursday 2pm at [address]. Equipment needed: X'

nodes.name: Evaluate Communication Cadence Rules
nodes.purpose: Nightly/hourly job: scan all active assignments and upcoming bookings against the org's cadence rules to generate and dispatch any due reminders.
nodes.ux_intent: The platform proactively prepares both worker and client for tomorrow's job — neither has to remember to check.
nodes.vertical_notes: Examples: 24h before job start (nanny/cleaner reminder), 1h before job start (en-route alert), day before credential expiry (worker alert), day after assignment complete (rating request).

nodes.name: Credential Expiry Alert
nodes.purpose: Alert both the worker and the admin when a credential (DBS, first aid cert, etc.) is approaching its expiry date, giving enough time to renew.
nodes.ux_intent: Worker receives a warm heads-up: 'Your First Aid certificate expires in 30 days. Tap here to upload your renewal.' Not a red warning — a helpful nudge.
nodes.vertical_notes: Critical for nannies — DBS, First Aid, and Paediatric First Aid all have fixed expiry. Expired credentials block new assignments. The alert prevents accidental suspension.

nodes.name: Payment Reminder
nodes.purpose: Send a payment reminder to a client (including anon clients) when an invoice is unpaid and approaching or past its due date.
nodes.ux_intent: The reminder reads politely — 'Just a reminder that your invoice for last week's care is due. Tap to pay.' Never aggressive, always easy to action.
nodes.vertical_notes: Anon clients receive payment reminders via email/SMS with their booking token — no login required to pay.
